# An attained ordinary minimum and its two-core quadrilateral stratum

This note concerns ordinary planar bodies with three fixed concurrent lines. It does not preserve neighboring mixed fibers or prove OC. It gives no classification of strata with three or more core equalities.

## 1. Fixed-area compactness

Use cyclic radii R=(A,B,t,a,b,r), endpoints (A,0),(0,B),(-t,t),(-a,0),(0,-b),(r,-r), and fixed positive sector areas W_i. Set c_i=1/(2W_i). The exact feasibility criterion requires the core inequalities R_i R_(i+1)<=2W_i and positive semidefiniteness of the matrix

    L_ii=c_(i-1)+c_i-1/R_i^2,
    L_(i,i+1)=c_i-1/(R_i R_(i+1)),

with all remaining off-diagonal entries zero. Write h_i=1/(R_i R_(i+1))-c_i>=0. A core sector is precisely h_i=0.

Assume at least one realizing body exists. Positive semidefiniteness gives the diagonal lower bounds

    R_i >= l_i := 1/sqrt(c_(i-1)+c_i)>0.

The next core inequality then gives R_i<=2W_i/l_(i+1). Thus every feasible radius vector lies in a fixed compact positive box. Within that box the core inequalities and matrix positive semidefiniteness are closed conditions, and the exact criterion realizes every feasible vector. Hence the feasible radius set is nonempty and compact.

For target chord ell=B+b, and other coarea chords ell_2=A+a, ell_3=t+r, its normalized inverse weight

    p=1/[1+ell(1/ell_2+1/ell_3)]

is continuous on this compact set. It attains a minimum. This is a finite-data attainment theorem; it does not require continuity of a particular polygon reconstruction as bodies vary.

The proved radius-monotonicity theorem shows that at such a minimum there is a core adjacent to node1 and a core adjacent to node4. Choose one from each pair. The four resulting edge pairs are (0,3),(0,4),(1,3),(1,4).

## 2. A rigidity lemma with zero excesses

Suppose feasible data have a strictly positive vector w with Lw=0. The body is uniquely determined by its endpoints and sector areas. Its vertices are precisely the inserted points belonging to the positive-excess sectors; in particular their number equals the number of h_i>0.

Here is the proof, including the zero-edge issue. For any exact one-extra-vertex realization let r_i,s_i be its harmonic charges, zero when h_i=0, and let delta_i be its nonnegative node slack. The audited exact Gram identity is

    x^T Lx=sum_i delta_i x_i^2
       +sum_(h_i>0)(s_i x_i-r_i x_(i+1))^2/(r_i+s_i).

Evaluation at w forces every delta_i=0 and fixes s_i w_i=r_i w_(i+1). The harmonic equality fixes both charges on every positive edge and therefore fixes its inserted point V_i. On a zero edge use V_i=(P_i+P_(i+1))/2; this is an interior point of the prescribed straight core edge and makes no geometrical choice. Each positive-edge block of L has a unique positive null vector up to scale, by the Gram ratios along its connected edges. Scaling a block does not change any inserted positive-edge vertex. Consequently the entire polygonal realization is unique.

Zero node slack makes V_(i-1),P_i,V_i collinear for every i. The exact convex realization and the distinct angular sectors place P_i strictly between its two neighboring inserted points. Thus no P_i is a vertex. An inserted point in a positive-excess sector is a strict vertex, since its turn determinant is D_i(t_i-1)>0 in the notation of the exact sector criterion. An inserted point in a zero-excess sector is not a vertex. This proves the asserted vertex count for the unique replacement polygon Q.

For an arbitrary actual realizing body K, choose one support at each P_i. The support-preserving replacement must equal Q. Each P_i is in the relative interior of an edge of Q, so its supporting line is unique. Every chosen support of K is therefore the corresponding edge line of Q. Every edge of Q contains at least one P_i, so their inward halfplanes intersect in Q and K is contained in Q. Both bodies have area sum W_i. Proper inclusion of full-dimensional compact convex bodies would leave positive area, so K=Q. No approximation or Hausdorff-local variation is used.

## 3. The stratum with exactly two core sectors

**Theorem.** At a fixed-W minimum of the target inverse weight, suppose exactly two sectors are cores. The actual realizing body is a unique quadrilateral. Its four vertices lie in the four positive-excess sectors.

The two core edges must be one of the four pairs listed in Section1; all other h_i are strictly positive. Removing these two zero edges splits L into two connected path blocks. A positive semidefinite connected path block that is singular has a strictly positive null vector: taking absolute values minimizes its least Rayleigh quotient, and its nonzero negative off-diagonal entries propagate positivity through the eigen-equations. It therefore suffices to show that both blocks are singular.

First take core edges0 and4. The blocks are {5,0} and {1,2,3,4}. If the first were positive definite, decrease R_0 slightly and increase R_1 so their product remains2W_0. The first block stays positive definite by continuity. In the second block, the diagonal entry at node1 and its adjacent negative off-diagonal entry both increase; the block remains a Z-matrix for a sufficiently small change because h_1>0. Entrywise increase of a PSD Z-matrix preserves PSD by the absolute-value quadratic-form argument. All remaining core inequalities remain valid. The target chord increases and the chord R_0+R_3 decreases, so p strictly decreases. This contradicts minimality. The short block is therefore singular.

If the long block were positive definite, decrease R_2 slightly, leaving all other radii fixed. Its incident edges1 and2 have positive excess, the core inequalities only improve, and the long block stays positive definite by continuity. The short block is unchanged. The chord R_2+R_5 decreases while the target chord is fixed, again strictly decreasing p. Thus the long block is singular as well.

For core edges1 and3, the short block is {2,3} and the long block is {4,5,0,1}. Decreasing R_2 and increasing R_1 while keeping their product2W_1 forces the short block to be singular by the same argument. Decreasing the free internal radius R_0 forces the long block to be singular.

For core edges0 and3, the blocks are {1,2,3} and {4,5,0}. Decreasing R_0 and increasing R_1 with product2W_0 proves singularity of {4,5,0}. Decreasing R_3 and increasing R_4 with product2W_3 proves singularity of {1,2,3}. In each operation the block of the decreased radius would remain positive definite if it started so, while the other block increases entrywise and retains its Z signs. The target chord increases and a different chord decreases.

For core edges1 and4, use the corresponding two operations R_2 down with R_1 up, and R_5 down with R_4 up. These prove singularity of {2,3,4} and {5,0,1}, respectively. Every perturbation is finite, sufficiently small, and preserves the two specified core products exactly; the four strict excesses supply all needed room for the changes.

Both blocks are consequently singular in every case. Concatenating their strictly positive null vectors gives a strictly positive null vector of L. Section2 now proves actual-body rigidity and the four-vertex conclusion.

This theorem does not assert that all minimizing data have exactly two cores. Additional simultaneous core equalities are genuine remaining strata. Nor does a quadrilateral here automatically satisfy the triangle Lorentz theorem or retain any mixed-fiber compatibility.
